headline: Woman kills daughter, dies by suicide in Tangail after family dispute
summary: A 25-year-old woman allegedly killed her four-year-old daughter before dying by suicide in Mirzapur, Tangail, following ongoing family disputes and financial hardships.
details: A tragic incident occurred in Mirzapur upazila of Tangail, where a 25-year-old woman, Konika Begum, allegedly killed her four-year-old daughter, Razia, before dying by suicide. The incident reportedly followed a prolonged family dispute.

Konika had married Rajib Hossain six years ago. Rajib was reportedly a drug user and frequently absent from home, leading to severe financial hardships and constant quarrels within the family. Disputes with her in-laws were also reported.

On Thursday night, Rajib left home after an argument and did not return. The next morning, Konika attempted to go to her father's house with Razia but was brought back by her father-in-law, Nazim Uddin.

Around 10:00 AM, Konika was discovered hanging from the ceiling of a room, while Razia was found dead on a bed. Police suspect Konika suffocated her daughter with a pillow before taking her own life. The bodies have been sent for autopsy to Tangail General Hospital.

headline_marked: UN warns of [[extremist cells in Bangladesh]]; police unaware
headline: UN warns of extremist cells in Bangladesh; police unaware
summary: The United Nations has raised concerns over the presence of extremist cells operating within the country, while local police remain unaware of their activities.
details: The United Nations has issued a warning regarding the existence of extremist cells operating within Bangladesh.
According to the UN, these cells are active and pose a potential risk to security.
The report highlights a concerning gap in intelligence, stating that local police forces are currently unaware of these specific groups.
The warning emphasizes the need for better monitoring and coordination to identify and the neutralize these threats before they can act.
caption:
The UN warns of hidden extremist cells in Bangladesh—and police don't know where they are.

The United Nations has issued a warning regarding the existence of extremist cells operating within Bangladesh.

According to the UN, these cells are active and pose a potential risk to security.

The report highlights a concerning gap in intelligence, stating that local police forces are currently unaware of these specific groups.

The warning emphasizes the need for better monitoring and coordination to identify and the neutralize these threats before they can act.
